title: AI Replacing Developers Has Officially Failed
summary: Sensational narrative that AI replacement 'failed' and companies are boomerang-rehiring; mixes real and shaky stats.

assertions.quote: Seasoned engineers were actually 19% slower when using AI tools

verdicts.note: Accurately reports METR's July 2025 RCT (16 devs, ~19% slower); the finding is specific to that setting and early-2025 tools.
METR RCT: 16 experienced developers, 246 tasks in their own mature repos; allowing early-2025 AI tools increased completion time by 19%.

assertions.quote: tech companies are desperate for human workers once again

verdicts.note: There are reports of AI-motivated cuts being reversed (e.g. Klarna support staff) and analyst forecasts of rehiring, but broad 'boomerang' rehiring of engineers is weakly evidenced.

assertions.quote: the tech market was utterly cooked before AI even stepped into the kitchen

verdicts.note: The 2022-23 decline began before ChatGPT and tracks rate hikes and over-hiring; most economists attribute it mainly to macro factors, though AI may weigh on junior roles since 2024.

assertions.quote: AI generated code has 1.7 times more errors compared to code written by human software engineers

verdicts.note: CodeRabbit's 2025 PR analysis found ~1.7x more issues in AI-authored PRs, and security studies agree; results depend heavily on review and tooling, and some studies find parity.
The Debt study explicitly does not compare AI commits with a human-only baseline, so it can't say whether AI code has more defects.

Using build success as a quality proxy, Copilot had no negative effect at Microsoft but a negative one at Accenture (-17.4%, p<0.05); pooled -5.5% NS, so evidence of more defects is mixed and the proxy is weak.
Peng et al. state explicitly that the study does not examine AI's effect on code quality, which could go either way.

METR 2025: raw AI output often needed major cleanup, but final AI-allowed PRs looked qualitatively similar in quality, and post-review fix time differed insignificantly (15 vs 9 min). Experienced reviewers caught defects before submission.
Defect risks are reported in 21% (10/47) of sources, discussed alongside productivity gains, but the review gives no human-written baseline and treats counts as mention frequency, not effect size.

In the RCT, ChatGPT access raised task accuracy by 26 percentage points (0.65 to about 0.91), and directly accepting AI output did not lower accuracy. The tasks were simple (GPT-4 solved them all), so this says little about defects in real code.

Across 470 open-source PRs, those with signals of AI co-authorship averaged 10.83 issues per PR against 6.45 for PRs assumed human-only (about 1.7x), by CodeRabbit's own issue taxonomy; a vendor report on a small sample that says it cannot guarantee the human-labelled PRs were human-only.

assertions.quote: AI generated code results in 38% more code volume

verdicts.note: GitClear and DORA 2025 data show more churn and duplication and lower delivery stability as AI adoption rises; more code means more to maintain.
Smells make up 89% of AI-introduced issues and pass review easily. The paper argues AI's higher speed and volume let these accumulate into a substantial maintenance burden.

assertions.quote: AI was a failed marketing scheme, not a full technical replacement

verdicts.note: Labs do have incentives and many evals are self-reported, but independent evals (METR, SWE-bench, LMArena) largely confirm capability gains.
Postings rose from the 2023 trough in some trackers (TrueUp, parts of Indeed), but remain far below 2022 and junior postings stayed weak; the data are mixed.

assertions.quote: This is one of the fastest growing roles in tech right now

verdicts.note: FDE postings grew several-fold in 2025 as AI labs and startups (OpenAI, Anthropic, Palantir-style firms) hired for them; still a small share of jobs.

assertions.quote: AI ended up creating more demand for humans not less

verdicts.note: Through 2026 evidence points to role change and slower junior hiring, not elimination of the profession; long-run is uncertain.
